A convention session of that kind seats on the order of five speakers, which puts presentations at roughly a sixth of a 1,500-person hall; I set the ratio at 17%. The relative +/-20% flex band is 13.6-20.4%, giving 204-306, nowhere near 800, and even at 50% — three times what the programme shape supports — this edition yields 750 and still falls short. This is the Chicago Dental Midwinter pattern from the methodology: a large professional convention whose contributed science is a small slice, judged small because little contributed science happens there, NOT because of who attends.

I put it at 90% rather than 100% because a share of the 650 are accompanying co-authors, exhibitors and organisers. The abstract ladder has nothing to work with: CIGR deposits no proceedings (the Crossref member registry returns only an unrelated CIGRE national committee for that query), the congress site is not on the society domain, and cigr.org links no programme or book of abstracts. What cigr.org does carry is the post-congress newsletter, linked straight from the homepage, which is a textbook A2 source — retrospective, by the organisers, accountable. Attendance 650+ from 60 countries, DELEGATES basis, three days. NOTE for Rupert: the 2026 edition was JOINT with EurAgEng (CIGR-EurAgEng World Congress 2026) and the 2030 edition is again joint with AgEng2030, so if EurAgEng ever gets its own row these must be counted once, not twice. Language: English only — CIGR's working language is English and its newsletter is published in English. Zero searches: found by following 지난 학술발표대회 from https://www.aik.or.kr/ (EUC-KR) to conf.aik.or.kr and then guessing the sibling edition slugs. Counted = 일반부문 소계 + 대학생부문 소계 = 403 + 68 = 471 for the largest edition (2024 autumn). Undergraduate posters are INCLUDED per field-notes counting rule 5 (a presenter is a presenter, as with KIEE's 학부생발표). EXCLUDED: 초청강연 (invited lectures, which have their own page), 특별세션, 위원회세션, 연구단세션 and 지회특별세미나 — organised/invited streams that the 발표편수 table already leaves out. Language: searched and read in KOREAN (학술발표대회, 발표편수, 구두발표, 포스터발표). Phase 1's hint of 800-1,500 per conference is not supported: the five editions I counted run 312-471.

character_evidence: An open 講演会 call producing a per-edition 講演会論文集 of contributed papers.
conference: JASNAOE Annual Meeting (Japan Society of Naval Architects and Ocean Engineers)
abstracts: 186 (largest edition, 2024 autumn; two editions per year)
spot_checks: Paged the J-STAGE search API past its 1,000-row cap and grouped prism:volume, having first confirmed every record's material_title is 日本船舶海洋工学会講演会論文集. Per-edition series: 2018 125/114, 2019 127/102, 2020 136/73, 2021 124/94, 2022 107/131, 2023 110/161, 2024 158/186, 2025 136/158. Two volumes per calendar year throughout, matching the 春季/秋季 pattern

Checked the society's separate Crossref deposit (member 1437, prefix 10.2534) to make sure the conference is not ALSO deposited there and being missed: that prefix holds only the peer-reviewed 日本船舶海洋工学会論文集 / Journal of Zosen Kiokai, running 23-49 items a year since 2015 — a different, much smaller publication, not the 講演会
cadence_evidence: https://www.jasnaoe.or.jp/lecture/archives.html lists 春季講演会 and 秋季講演会 for every year from 平成18 (2006) to 令和8 (2026), and the J-STAGE proceedings carry exactly two volume numbers per calendar year. Two editions a year.
method: Rung 4, J-STAGE deposit index, zero searches. The proceedings are 日本船舶海洋工学会講演会論文集, whose J-STAGE journal code is `conf` — found by following 講演会論文集バックナンバー（J-STAGEへリンクします）from https://www.jasnaoe.or.jp/lecture/archives.html to https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/browse/conf/list/-char/ja, NOT by guessing. Counted per edition by grouping on prism:volume (one volume per 講演会). Largest recent edition = 186 papers (vol 39, 2024 autumn); the eight-year series never exceeds 186 and the per-edition mean is about 130. This is the society's own complete proceedings of the meeting, not a partial deposit, so it is a real count rather than a floor. Far below the 800 cutoff. Excluded: nothing needed — the 論文集 carries contributed papers only. Language: searched and read in JAPANESE (講演会 / 講演会論文集). Phase 1's 'several hundred presentations; likely below the bar' is confirmed, at the low end.

character_evidence: An open call for papers with Springer-published full-paper proceedings per edition.
conference: ICPR - International Conference on Production Research
spot_checks: Springer's own conference-series index for the International Conference on Production Research prints the paper count per proceedings volume. ICPR 2025 (12-17 July, Chia, Colombia), 'Sustainable Systems in an Internetworked Digital World': 61 papers, 1 volume. ICPR Americas 2022 (Curitiba), 11th edition: 90 papers. ICPR 2021 (Taichung), 'Systems Collaboration and Integration': 27 papers. ISPR 2019 (Vienna): 69 papers

Checked the IFPR side too: ifpr.org is a parked domain that redirects to /lander, and the regional editions run on their own short-lived sites (ifpr-icpra2024.org, icpramericas2026.org, events.polyu.edu.hk/icprapr2025). The series is fragmented into ICPR, ICPR Americas and ICPR Asia-Pacific, each a separate small meeting

DISAMBIGUATION TRAP: 'ICPR' in Springer is overwhelmingly the International Conference on PATTERN RECOGNITION (link.springer.com/conference/icpr), a large computer-vision conference that is a different meeting entirely and belongs to CS if anywhere. The production-research series is link.springer.com/conference/icpr1 — the trailing 1 is load-bearing
cadence_evidence: The Springer series shows ICPR volumes for 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2025, i.e. roughly every second year once the regional editions are separated out; the queue's biennial reading holds. 0.5.
method: Rung 4, the publisher's own series index, one search (English; the conference is English-language and the local-language rule does not bite). The figure is the count Springer prints for the volume, cross-read against three sibling editions. Even treating the Springer volume as a FLOOR — some presentations may not be written up — the series runs 27-90 papers per edition, an order of magnitude below the 800 cutoff, so no floor multiple could carry it. Phase 1's 'several hundred papers' hint is not supported by any edition since 2019. Phase 1 also cited faimconference.org, which is the FAIM conference, a DIFFERENT meeting that shares some of IFPR's community; I did not use it.

character_evidence: Open abstract submission with acceptance notification (soft2024.eu/abstract-submission/ and /item/acceptance-of-abstract/), producing a poster-dominated contributed programme; papers then appear in a Fusion Engineering and Design special issue.
conference: SOFT - Symposium on Fusion Technology
abstracts: 757 (640 onsite posters + 54 virtual posters + 63 contributed orals)
spot_checks: Downloaded the final SOFT 2024 programme booklet into my own directory (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 9,616,471 bytes) and extracted with BOTH pdftotext modes. Unique IDs, IDENTICAL in -layout and -raw: posters P<n>-<m> 640, virtual posters VP-<n> 54, contributed orals O<n><X>.<m> 63, invited talks IT<n><X>.<m> 21

Sanity-checked the poster count against the printed session structure: four onsite poster sessions numbered P1..P4 with the highest observed ID P4-159, i.e. about 160 boards per session x 4 = 640, which is what the union gives

EXCLUDED the 21 IT-prefixed invited talks and the five plenary sessions, both of which the booklet labels separately; the booklet's own wording is 'include invited, oral and poster presentations', so the invited exclusion is done on the organiser's own labels rather than by inference
cadence_evidence: SOFT 2024 Dublin is the 33rd symposium and the series is biennial (32nd in 2022, 34th in 2026). 0.5.
method: Rung 3, counting the programme booklet, one search. Route: the Fourwaves event (event.fourwaves.com/soft2024) is a Nuxt SPA whose public API I did reach — https://api.fourwaves.com/api/events/soft2024 returns the event JSON, and /api/events/<uuid>/sessions returns the 38 sessions — but its 'Presentations' page has scope 'participants' and /api/agenda returns 401, which is a CREDENTIAL wall, not rung 5, so per the brief I went looking for another artefact instead. One search located soft2024.eu; the domain no longer resolves, so I enumerated it with Wayback CDX and pulled the final programme booklet of 19 September 2024. Counted 640 + 54 + 63 = 757 contributed presentations. Note this row sits just under the line and should be seen knowingly: 757 is 43 short of the 800 cutoff on a count that is exact and reproduced identically by two extractions, so it is OUT on positive evidence rather than on absence of it, but a single edition's growth would move it. DISAGREEMENT recorded, not resolved: a trade report of the meeting states about 1,000 participants, which is attendance, not presentations. Language: English only — SOFT is an English-language European symposium.

character_evidence: OCEANS runs an open call for papers and every accepted paper appears in IEEE Xplore; the deposit is the contributed technical programme.
conference: OCEANS Conference
abstracts: 418 (largest single edition; two editions per year)
spot_checks: Container facet, double-unescaped, per year: 'OCEANS 2023 - Limerick' 418; 'OCEANS 2024 - Halifax' 368 and 'OCEANS 2024 - Singapore' 331; 'OCEANS 2025 Brest' 417
Applied the two-meetings-a-year rule: 2024 shows both editions explicitly (Halifax 368 + Singapore 331), so the per-edition figure is reported and the 699 sum is NOT used
cadence_evidence: 2024 carries two distinct OCEANS containers in the same year, Halifax (MTS/IEEE, autumn, Americas) and Singapore (spring, Asia-Pacific), which is the long-standing two-editions-a-year pattern of the joint IEEE OES / Marine Technology Society series. events_per_yr = 2.
method: Rung 4, Crossref publisher deposit index via the IEEE container facet, zero searches. Per field-notes 2.1 the figure is the exact container facet, read after double HTML-unescaping the keys. Largest single edition found in 2023-2025 is 418 (Limerick 2023); no edition exceeds 418. IEEE requires a paper for every presentation, so this is near-complete, not a floor. Per the brief's two-meetings-a-year rule the per-edition figure is reported with events_per_yr = 2, never the annual sum. Excluded: nothing. Language: English only — OCEANS is an English-language IEEE/MTS conference.
